correctness.rationale: The exact normalized fourth moment equals both the sum of squared aperiodic autocorrelations (10 positive shifts plus zero) and the sum of squared coefficients of the squared Fourier polynomial. Gauge action c_jk→lambda alpha^j beta^k c_jk acts freely and uniquely fixes coordinates (0,0),(0,1),(1,0), reducing every q-phase array bijectively to q^5 choices, q in {2,3,4,6}. A standalone standard-library program recalculates both exact integer formulas on all 32+243+1024+7776=9075 representatives, verifies every moment histogram, all minimizers and their orbit partitions against an independently stored exact certificate. It finds minima 88,84,88,84, second distinct values 96,96,92,86 and optimizer totals 48,54,896,3024. Arithmetic is exact in Gaussian or Eisenstein rings; no sampling inference is made. For any finite Fourier torus with horizontal size≥7 and vertical size≥3, all degrees in P squared (0..6,0..2) are nonaliased, proving transfer by Parseval. Supplementary direct complex finite-grid checks on 48 sampled arrays agreed with the exact calculation. No claim outside four alphabets and the specified support.

Four natural practical phase alphabets have distinct optimal performance and different positive spectral gaps: ternary and six-phase attain 84 versus 88 for binary and quaternary, a nonmonotone alphabet-versus-angle phenomenon, and every optimizer is classified up to conjugation, coordinate reversal and phase characters. The exact nonoptimal gaps and complete equality classification are natural discrete design invariants. The same sharp conclusions hold on every sufficiently large finite Fourier sampling grid by an analytic no-alias argument. This is a meaningful bounded full classification, not a random slice or a claimed asymptotic general theorem.
